all.name: Sets and counting principles
all.description: Set notation, Venn diagrams, inclusion-exclusion and the rule of product.
objectives: use set notation for union, intersection and complement
visualize set operations with Venn diagrams
apply inclusion-exclusion to count elements
apply the rule of product to count outcomes

all.name: Independence of events
all.description: Defining and checking independence of events and its paradoxes.
objectives: state the definition of independent events
check whether two events are independent
explain why a probability-zero event is independent of itself

all.name: Random variables, pmf and cdf
all.description: Random variables as payoff functions and their probability mass and cumulative distribution functions.
objectives: define a discrete random variable on a sample space
write the pmf of a random variable
compute and graph a cdf
state properties of the cdf

all.name: Repeated updating and screening
all.description: Updating posteriors with successive data and revisiting the base rate fallacy.
objectives: use a posterior as the next prior
update on multiple data points at once
solve a screening test example with a Bayes table

all.name: Bayesian updating with Bayes tables
all.description: Use a coin example to define hypotheses, data, prior, likelihood and posterior and compute them in a Bayes table.
objectives: identify prior, likelihood and posterior in a problem
build a Bayes table for discrete hypotheses
express priors and posteriors as pmfs
distinguish probability of data from probability of hypotheses

all.name: Conditional probability and multiplication rule
all.description: Defines conditional probability and derives the multiplication rule from it.
objectives: compute a conditional probability from the definition
apply the multiplication rule to find joint probabilities
interpret conditioning as restricting the sample space

all.name: Bayes' theorem and base rate fallacy
all.description: Introduces Bayes' theorem for inverting conditional probabilities and illustrates the base rate fallacy with screening tests.
objectives: state and derive Bayes' theorem
invert a conditional probability
explain the base rate fallacy
compute the probability of disease given a positive test

all.name: Law of total probability and trees
all.description: Partition the sample space and organize conditional probability computations with urn models and trees.
objectives: state the law of total probability for a partition
compute probabilities in urn problems
organize a multi-stage computation with a probability tree
distinguish shorthand from precise tree labels

all.name: Arithmetic with random variables
all.description: Shows how to add, multiply and transform random variables and count with sums of indicator variables.
objectives: compute the pmf of a sum of random variables
use indicator sums to count successes
find the distribution of a function of a random variable

all.name: Bernoulli and binomial distributions
all.description: Model single trials and counts of successes in independent trials, and derive the binomial pmf.
objectives: write the pmf of a Bernoulli(p) variable
compute binomial probabilities
explain the binomial coefficient in the pmf
recognize when a binomial model applies

all.name: Geometric, uniform and other distributions
all.description: Model waiting times with the geometric distribution, equally likely outcomes with the uniform distribution, and look up other named distributions.
objectives: compute geometric probabilities for tails before first head
write the pmf of a discrete uniform variable
explore distributions with the applet
look up an unfamiliar pmf in a reference

all.name: Comparison model search lower bound
all.description: Uses decision trees to show comparison-based search needs Omega(log n) time.
objectives: describe the comparison model of computation
model an algorithm as a decision tree
derive the Omega(log n) lower bound for comparison search
explain why the bound motivates non-comparison data structures

all.name: Direct access arrays and hash tables
all.description: Builds hash tables from direct access arrays, resolving collisions by chaining and choosing good hash functions.
objectives: implement a set with a direct access array
explain hash functions and collisions
analyze chaining under a universal hash family
maintain hash table size dynamically with amortized rebuilds

all.name: Priority queues and PQ sort
all.description: Introduces the priority queue interface and compares AVL, array, and sorted array implementations via priority queue sort.
objectives: state the priority queue operations
turn any priority queue into a sorting algorithm
compare running times of array, sorted array, and AVL priority queues
relate selection and insertion sort to priority queue sort

all.name: Binary heap operations and heap sort
all.description: Implements max-heaps on implicit complete binary trees and uses them for in-place heap sort and linear build.
objectives: compute parent and child indices in an implicit tree
perform heap insert with max heapify up
perform delete max with max heapify down
run in-place heap sort
prove linear-time heap build

all.name: SRT BOT and longest common subsequence
all.description: Reviews dynamic programming steps and applies them to the longest common subsequence problem.
objectives: list the SRT BOT steps
define subproblems over prefixes and suffixes
write the LCS recurrence
analyze LCS running time

all.name: LIS, coin game, subproblem expansion
all.description: Solves longest increasing subsequence and the alternating coin game using constrained and expanded subproblems.
objectives: solve LIS with a constrained subproblem
model the coin game with substring subproblems
expand subproblems with extra state such as whose turn
decide when to constrain or expand subproblems
